sourceFacts.fact: Nasolacrimal obstruction prevents normal tear drainage, causing tears to build up and overflow.
Watery eyes and discharge from obstruction do not require increased tear production; infection remains a clinical differential.

layoutSpecification: Title 'Tear production and drainage'. Side-by-side balance metaphor with two identical simple open ceramic bowls, no eyes or anatomical channels. In BOTH panels exactly three teal drops descend from above under a shared bracket 'Same tear input'. LEFT heading 'Usual drainage': bowl water low; open short abstract outlet on bowl's lower right lets blue drops leave into a small puddle, arrow points OUTWARD. RIGHT heading 'Poor drainage': same bowl outlet visibly capped with an ochre stop symbol; water rises to rim and drops spill OVER the outer rim, labelled 'Overflow'. No outward flow through the capped outlet. Bottom 'Abstract balance model'. Keep same incoming drop count and clear difference at outlets; this visual explains poor drainage, not a clinical test or increased tear production.
